title: Get a dog license
question: My dog is older than four months. How do I get or renew a Staunton dog license?
summary: Every dog 4 months or older owned by someone living in the City of Staunton needs a city dog license and a current rabies vaccination (or a health department exemption). State law allows 30 days after the dog turns 4 months or comes to you. The City Treasurer sells one-, two- or three-year licenses ($10, $15 or $20), up to the year the rabies certificate expires. Mail the rabies certificate and a check to City Treasurer, P.O. Box 474, Staunton, VA 24402, and the tag comes by mail, or bring the certificate to the Treasurer's office on the first floor of City Hall. Renew by January 31 of the year the rabies certificate expires. Trained guide, hearing and service dogs pay no tax.

legal_basis.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person other than a releasing agency that has registered as such annually with local animal control to own a dog four months old or older in the Commonwealth unless such dog is licensed, as required by the provisions of this article.

"Releasing agency" means (i) a public animal shelter or (ii) a private animal shelter, humane society, animal welfare organization, society for the prevention of cruelty to animals, or other similar entity or home-based rescue that releases companion animals for adoption.
"Owner" means any person who: (i) has a right of property in an animal; (ii) keeps or harbors an animal; (iii) has an animal in his care; or (iv) acts as a custodian of an animal.
The governing body of each county or city shall impose by ordinance a license tax on the ownership of dogs within its jurisdiction.
The tax for each dog or cat shall not be more than $10 for each year or $50 for a lifetime license
The governing body may establish different rates of taxation for ownership of female dogs, male dogs, spayed or neutered dogs, female cats, male cats, and spayed or neutered cats.

No license tax shall be levied on any dog that is trained and serves as (i) a guide dog for a blind person, (ii) a hearing dog for a person who is deaf or hard of hearing, or (iii) a service dog for a mobility-impaired or otherwise disabled person.
The provision of emotional support, well-being, comfort, or companionship shall not constitute work or tasks for the purposes of this definition.
A locality may by ordinance exempt any dog that served as a police or law-enforcement dog or military working dog from the license tax provided in subsection A.
Any ordinance may provide for an annual license tax for kennels of 10, 20, 30, 40, or 50 dogs or cats not to exceed $50 for any one such block of kennels.
"Kennel" means any establishment in which five or more canines, felines, or hybrids of either are kept for the purpose of breeding, hunting, training, renting, buying, boarding, selling, or showing.
The owner or custodian of all dogs and cats four months of age and older shall have such animal currently vaccinated for rabies

The supervising veterinarian on the premises shall provide the owner or custodian of the dog or the cat with a rabies vaccination certificate or herd rabies vaccination certificate and shall keep a copy in his own files.
such exemption shall be considered in place of a current certificate of vaccination
A dog or cat license shall consist of a license receipt and a metal tag.

No license tag shall be issued for any dog or cat unless there is presented, to the treasurer or other officer of the locality, or other agent charged by law with the duty of issuing license tags for dogs and cats, satisfactory evidence that such dog or cat has been inoculated or vaccinated against rabies

by making oral or written application to the treasurer of the locality where such person resides, accompanied by the amount of license tax and current certificate of vaccination as required by this article or satisfactory evidence that such certificate has been obtained

shall only have authority to license dogs and cats of resident owners or custodians who reside within the boundary limits of his county or city and may require information to this effect from any applicant
shall issue a license receipt for the amount on which he shall record the name and address of the owner or custodian, the date of payment, the years for which issued, the serial number of the tag
The information thus received shall be retained by the treasurer, open to public inspection, during the period for which such license is valid.
The treasurer may establish substations in convenient locations in the county or city and appoint agents for the collection of the license tax and issuance of such licenses.

The veterinarian shall forward within 45 days a copy of the rabies vaccination certificate or the relevant information contained in such certificate to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination occurs.

has failed to apply for a license within 90 days of the date of vaccination, the treasurer shall transmit an application to the owner and request the owner to submit a completed application and pay the appropriate fee
The treasurer shall remit any rabies vaccination certificate received for any animal owned by an individual residing in another locality to the local treasurer for the appropriate locality.

The license tax as prescribed in § 3.2-6528 is due not later than 30 days after a dog or cat has reached the age of four months, or not later than 30 days after an owner acquires a dog or cat four months of age or older, and each year thereafter.
Licensing periods for individual dogs and cats may be equal to and may run concurrently with the rabies vaccination effective period.
Any kennel license tax prescribed pursuant to § 3.2-6528 shall be due on January 1 and not later than January 31 of each year.
Dog license tags shall be securely fastened to a substantial collar by the owner or custodian and worn by such dog.
Dog and cat license receipts shall be carefully preserved by the licensees and exhibited promptly on request for inspection by any animal control officer or other officer.
It shall be unlawful for the owner to permit any licensed dog four months old or older to run or roam at large at any time without a license tag.
The fee for a duplicate tag for any dog or cat shall not exceed $1.
Any dog or cat not wearing a collar bearing a valid license tag shall prima facie be deemed to be unlicensed
The following shall be unlawful acts and are Class 4 misdemeanors
For any dog or cat owner to fail to pay any license tax required by this chapter before February 1 for the year in which it is due.
For any person to make a false statement in order to secure a dog or cat license to which he is not entitled.
For any person to conceal or harbor any dog or cat on which any required license tax has not been paid.
Any other violation of this chapter for which a specific penalty is not provided.
For Class 4 misdemeanors, a fine of not more than $250.

Payment of the license tax subsequent to a summons to appear before a court for failure to pay the license tax within the time required shall not operate to relieve such owner from the penalties or court costs
shall require dogs running at large without the tag required by § 3.2-6531 or in violation of an ordinance passed pursuant to § 3.2-6538 to be confined therein

In addition to this and any other fees that might be levied, the locality may, after a public hearing, adopt an ordinance to charge the owner of an animal a fee for impoundment and increased fees for subsequent impoundments of the same animal.

If an animal confined pursuant to this section has not been claimed upon expiration of the applicable stray hold period as provided by subsection C, it shall be deemed abandoned and become the property of the public animal shelter.
The local health director, in consultation with the state public health veterinarian, may grant an exemption to the requirement for rabies vaccination
if a vaccination would likely endanger the animal's life due to a previously diagnosed disease or other previously documented medical considerations as documented by a licensed veterinarian

Such exemption may be granted for an individual animal only after the veterinarian has (i) consulted with the local health director and completed and submitted to the LHD an application for exemption from rabies vaccination on a form approved by the department and (ii) submitted other documents or medical records as may be requested by the LHD.

Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination may be presented in lieu of a rabies vaccination certificate for the purposes of veterinary inspection by designated local authorities and for the purposes of licensing by the locality where the animal resides.

Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination shall be valid for one year, after which time the animal shall be vaccinated against rabies or the application for exemption shall be renewed.

steps.step: Check whether your dog needs a Staunton license
steps.who: The dog's owner or custodian who lives inside the City of Staunton
steps.how: Every dog 4 months old or older must be licensed. Under state law an 'owner' includes anyone who keeps, harbors or cares for the dog. Registered releasing agencies (shelters and rescues registered with local animal control) are exempt. Trained guide, hearing and service dogs still get a license but pay no tax (see s4). The City Treasurer licenses only dogs of owners who live within the city limits. If you live in Augusta County, even with a Staunton mailing address, license the dog with your county treasurer instead.
steps.deadline: Not later than 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old, or not later than 30 days after you acquire a dog 4 months old or older (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A))
steps.quote: If you own a dog that is older than four months, a dog license and rabies vaccination are required by Virginia Law and Staunton City Code.

steps.step: Have the dog vaccinated against rabies and keep the certificate
steps.who: Owner; a licensed veterinarian (or a licensed veterinary technician under a veterinarian's direct supervision)
steps.how: The veterinarian gives you a rabies vaccination certificate. It shows when the vaccination expires, and that date decides how many years of license you can buy (s4). By law the veterinarian also sends a copy (or its details) to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination happens, within 45 days. The Treasurer will not issue a tag without satisfactory evidence of rabies vaccination.
steps.deadline: The dog must be currently vaccinated from 4 months of age (Va. Code § 3.2-6521(A))
steps.quote: The supervising veterinarian on the premises shall provide the owner or custodian of the dog or the cat with a rabies vaccination certificate or herd rabies vaccination certificate and shall keep a copy in his own files.

steps.step: Only if the dog cannot safely be vaccinated: get a rabies vaccination exemption certificate
steps.who: Your veterinarian applies; the local health director (Virginia Department of Health, Central Shenandoah Health District, which serves Staunton), in consultation with the state public health veterinarian, decides
steps.how: Only a dog whose vaccination would likely endanger its life, because of a previously diagnosed disease or other medical considerations documented by a licensed veterinarian, qualifies. The veterinarian consults the local health director, completes and submits the Department of Health exemption request form (f1), and sends any other documents or medical records the health director asks for. If the exemption is approved, the health department issues an exemption certificate, with copies to the veterinarian, the owner and the animal control office of the locality where the owner lives. State law says the exemption counts in place of a current vaccination certificate for licensing. The Staunton Dog License page does not mention exemptions, so tell the Treasurer's office when you apply.
steps.deadline: The exemption certificate is valid for one year; then the dog must be vaccinated or the exemption renewed (12VAC5-105-30(B))
steps.quote: Certification that a dog or cat is exempt from rabies vaccination may be presented in lieu of a rabies vaccination certificate for the purposes of veterinary inspection by designated local authorities and for the purposes of licensing by the locality where the animal resides.

steps.step: Choose how many years to license and work out the fee
steps.how: Staunton sells licenses for one, two or three years, but only up to and including the year the dog's rabies certificate expires. The page shows one price per dog, with no different rate for spayed or neutered dogs. A trained guide dog, hearing dog or service dog pays no license tax under state law. An emotional support or comfort animal is not a service dog. The Dog License page does not mention this exemption, so tell the Treasurer's office if it applies.
steps.fee: One year: $10; two years: $15; three years: $20; no tax for a trained guide, hearing or service dog
steps.quote: You may purchase licenses up to and including the year that the rabies certificate expires.

steps.step: Apply by mail: send the rabies certificate and a check to the City Treasurer
steps.how: Mail a valid rabies certificate and a check for the fee to City Treasurer, P.O. Box 474, Staunton, VA 24402. The Treasurer's office mails the dog tag back to you. The Dog License page names no application form. State law allows an oral or written application, and the license receipt records the owner's name and address and the dog's sex and spay or neuter status, so a short note with those details may help the office. The page does not say who to make the check payable to or whether to send the original certificate or a copy; ask the office at 540.332.3833.
steps.deadline: Not later than 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old or is acquired (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A))
steps.fee: $10 (one year), $15 (two years) or $20 (three years), by check
steps.quote: By Mail: Send a valid rabies certificate and a check with the applicable fee to

steps.step: Or apply in person at the Treasurer's office in City Hall
steps.how: Bring a valid rabies certificate and the fee to the Treasurer's office, City Hall, first floor (Beverley Street entrance), 116 W. Beverley Street. The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday. The Dog License page does not say which forms of payment the counter takes for dog licenses. The City's online and pay-by-phone services list only real estate tax, personal property tax and utility bills, so no online dog license purchase was found.
steps.deadline: Not later than 30 days after the dog turns 4 months old or is acquired (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A))
steps.quote: In-Person: Bring a valid rabies certificate to the Treasurer’s office, located at

steps.step: The Treasurer checks the certificate and residence, then issues the license receipt and metal tag
steps.how: The Treasurer may license only dogs whose owners live in the city and may require information showing that from any applicant. With a proper application and a current vaccination certificate, the Treasurer records the owner's name and address, the payment date, the years the license covers, the tag's serial number and the dog's sex and spay or neuter status, and gives you a license receipt and a metal tag. These license records are open to public inspection while the license is valid. For a mailed application the tag comes back by mail; the page gives no processing time.
steps.quote: shall issue a license receipt for the amount on which he shall record the name and address of the owner or custodian, the date of payment, the years for which issued, the serial number of the tag

steps.step: Put the tag on the dog's collar and keep the receipt
steps.how: Fasten the tag to a sturdy collar that the dog wears. It is unlawful to let a licensed dog 4 months or older run or roam at large without its license tag. Keep the license receipt and show it if an animal control officer or other officer asks. State law lets the collar and tag come off while the dog is lawfully hunting, competing in a dog show, confined, under your immediate control, or has a skin condition a collar would worsen. A dog without a tag is presumed unlicensed. Staunton animal control officers do license and vaccination checks, and a dog impounded without a current city license costs an extra $15 to reclaim.
steps.quote: Dogs are required by law to be licensed and to wear identification when outside of the presence of their owners.

steps.step: If you have not applied, expect a license application from the Treasurer
steps.how: Veterinarians must send rabies certificate information to the treasurer of the locality where the vaccination happens, and a treasurer passes on certificates for dogs whose owners live in another locality. If the Treasurer finds from that information that the owner of an unlicensed dog has not applied for a license within 90 days of the vaccination, state law has the Treasurer send the owner an application and ask for the fee. Complete it and pay as in s5 or s6. This follow-up does not extend the 30-day deadline in s1. The Staunton pages do not describe this follow-up, so it is given here from state law only.
steps.deadline: The Treasurer's follow-up comes when no application has been made within 90 days of the date of vaccination (Va. Code § 3.2-6529(B)); the owner's own deadline is still 30 days (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(A))
steps.quote: has failed to apply for a license within 90 days of the date of vaccination, the treasurer shall transmit an application to the owner and request the owner to submit a completed application and pay the appropriate fee

steps.step: Renew the license when it runs out
steps.how: Get the dog's rabies vaccination renewed before the old certificate expires, then renew the license by mail or in person as in s5 or s6 with the new certificate. You can again buy up to three years, but not past the year the new certificate expires. The Treasurer's page sets the renewal date as January 31 of the year the rabies certificate expires. State law makes it a Class 4 misdemeanor to fail to pay a license tax before February 1 of the year it is due.
steps.deadline: By January 31 of the year the rabies vaccination certificate expires (City Treasurer's Dog License page)
steps.quote: You must renew your dog license by Jan. 31 of the year the rabies vaccination certificate expires via mail or in person at the Treasurer’s office.

steps.step: Replace a lost, destroyed or stolen tag
steps.who: Owner or custodian; City Treasurer's Office
steps.how: Apply to the Treasurer's office for a duplicate tag and show the original license receipt. State law has the owner make an affidavit (a sworn statement) before the Treasurer that the tag was lost, destroyed or stolen. The Treasurer notes the duplicate's number and date on the original receipt. Put the new tag on the collar right away. The City Code has a duplicate-tag section (§ 6.10.160), but no Staunton page states the fee; state law caps it at $1.
steps.deadline: At once, as the statute states (Va. Code § 3.2-6532)
steps.fee: Not stated by the City; not more than $1 under state law
steps.quote: If a dog or cat license tag is lost, destroyed or stolen, the owner or custodian shall at once apply to the treasurer or his agent who issued the original license for a duplicate license tag, presenting the original license receipt.

steps.step: Kennels only: ask the Treasurer about a kennel license
steps.who: Kennel operator (under the state definition, an establishment in which five or more dogs are kept for breeding, hunting, training, renting, buying, boarding, selling or showing; the City Code's own definition was not read); City Treasurer's Office
steps.how: The City Code has a kennel license section (§ 6.10.180), but the Treasurer's Dog License page does not mention kennels or give a kennel fee. Ask the Treasurer's office how to apply and what it costs. State law caps a kennel tax at $50 for each block of 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 dogs and makes it due in January.
steps.deadline: Due on January 1 and not later than January 31 of each year (Va. Code § 3.2-6530(C))
steps.fee: Not stated by the City; not more than $50 per block under state law
steps.quote: Any kennel license tax prescribed pursuant to § 3.2-6528 shall be due on January 1 and not later than January 31 of each year.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Dog License page text is the same in copies from November 2021, April 2023, September 2025, February 2026 and July 2026. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Other addresses. https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/i-want-to-/apply-for/dog-license redirects (through /?navid=298) to the Treasurer's Dog License page, and https://www.ci.staunton.va.us/residents/dog-licenses is a menu link to the same place. All three addresses therefore lead to one page.

Local ordinance not checked or quoted. The Staunton City Code is on General Code's eCode360, whose terms limit content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes. Only the headings of Title 6 and Chapter 6.10 (Dogs and Cats) have been checked, for section numbers and links (Article II, License, §§ 6.10.070 to 6.10.180). The section text has not been checked. The citations' descriptions are lexflow's paraphrases of the headings. So the ordinance's tax amounts, due date, penalty, kennel fee and duplicate-tag fee are not confirmed, and the fees here are those the Treasurer publishes. City Council agenda packets have not been searched for the ordinance: the city site refuses automated readers and the Internet Archive has no full-text search.

Renewal date wording. The Dog License page says to renew 'by Jan. 31 of the year the rabies vaccination certificate expires'. It does not say when a license ends. State law makes the tax due 'each year thereafter', lets licensing periods run with the rabies vaccination period (§ 3.2-6530(A)), and makes it a misdemeanor not to pay before February 1 of the year the tax is due (§ 3.2-6587(A)(2)). Read together, Staunton licenses seem to run by calendar year, but the end date of a license and exactly when a renewal is due were not confirmed. Ask the Treasurer's office.

No application form. The Dog License page names no form. For mail it asks only for a valid rabies certificate and a check. It does not say whether to send the original certificate or a copy, who the check is payable to, or what owner details to include. State law allows an oral or written application (§ 3.2-6527).

Payment. The Dog License page mentions only a check for mail. It does not say which payment types the counter takes for dog licenses. The City's online and pay-by-phone services list only real estate tax, personal property tax and utility bills, and the card fee schedule lists only those. The green drop box on Central Avenue takes 'ALL city payments' by check or money order, but no page says it may be used for a dog license, which needs the rabies certificate too. The Paying Taxes & Fees page's HTML also carries an older block inside an HTML comment, which readers do not see, that says the City cannot take card payments in person. Because it is not displayed it was not relied on; ask the office which payment types the counter takes.

Rate options. Staunton's page shows one price per dog for each term, with no separate rate by sex or spay or neuter status, though state law allows different rates (§ 3.2-6528(A)). No lifetime license is offered on the page; state law lets a locality offer one for up to $50 (§§ 3.2-6528(A), 3.2-6530(B)). The two- and three-year prices ($15 and $20) are below the $10-a-year cap.

Exemptions not on the city page. The Dog License page does not mention the state service-dog exemption, the rabies medical exemption certificate, or the local option to exempt retired police and military dogs (§ 3.2-6528(B)). The first two apply under state law by their own terms. Whether Staunton has adopted the police and military dog exemption is not known. The Central Shenandoah Health District serves Staunton, but no rabies exemption contact was found on its pages read; the veterinarian makes the request.

Veterinarian reports. State law requires veterinarians to send rabies certificate information to the treasurer where the vaccination happens, and the treasurer to mail an application if no license follows within 90 days (§ 3.2-6529). The Staunton pages do not describe whether or how the Treasurer does this.

Residence. The City Treasurer can license only dogs of owners who live inside the city (§ 3.2-6527). Staunton is an independent city surrounded by Augusta County, and some Staunton mailing addresses are in the county. Augusta County's dog license process is not covered here. Neither state law nor the City pages give an explicit deadline for someone who moves into Staunton with a dog licensed elsewhere; the 30-day rule in § 3.2-6530(A) is written for dogs reaching 4 months or being acquired.

Penalties. Owning an unlicensed dog is unlawful (§ 3.2-6524(A)). Under § 3.2-6587(A), failing to pay the license tax before February 1 of the year it is due ((A)(2)), concealing or harboring a dog whose license tax is unpaid ((A)(7)), and any other violation of the chapter for which no specific penalty is provided ((A)(9)) are Class 4 misdemeanors, punishable by a fine of up to $250 (§ 18.2-11(d)); for (A)(2) the court may also order the dog confiscated. Which subdivision, or which City Code section, a Staunton summons for an unlicensed dog would cite was not confirmed. Paying after a summons does not avoid the penalty or court costs (§ 3.2-6536). The Animal Control page says owners face summonses and fines of up to $250 for the city animal rules it lists. City Code § 6.10.110 (failure to pay tax when due) was not read.

Impound fees. The Animal Control page lists fees 'set by City ordinance' but does not name the section. Its $25 item speaks of a 'vaccination tag' not fastened to a collar; whether that also covers the license tag is not stated. It also says an animal without proof of current rabies vaccination and a City license 'will pay an additional penalty'. Fees are paid when reclaiming the animal; the page says the shelter keeps the City of Waynesboro's schedule. The page lists five impound fees; all five are in fees. By the eCode360 headings, Article III of Chapter 6.10 has § 6.10.210 (impoundment generally; public animal shelter designated), § 6.10.220 (impoundment and disposition of animals) and § 6.10.230 (prosecution of owner redeeming dog). Their text was not read, so which section sets the impound fees, and whether an owner who reclaims an unlicensed dog may also be prosecuted under the City Code, are not confirmed.

City Code citations on the Animal Control page. The page cites City Code 6.10.010 and 6.10.190 for the rule that dogs be vaccinated and licensed (its sentence reads 'dogs must be license by the City Treasurer', as quoted). By the eCode360 headings, § 6.10.190 is about running at large and the license article is §§ 6.10.070 to 6.10.180, so the page's citation may be loose or out of date.

Cats. No Staunton cat license was found on the pages read. Chapter 6.10 covers dogs and cats, but from the headings alone it cannot be said whether Article II licenses cats. The Animal Control page says all cats must wear a rabies tag on their collar. Cat licensing is a local option (§ 3.2-6524(B)).

No administrative appeal of a Treasurer licensing decision was found, in state law or on the City pages. The Treasurer is an elected constitutional officer. No page or statute sets a time for the Treasurer to issue a license or mail a tag. Refund provisions for erroneously assessed local taxes in Title 58.1 are written for taxes assessed by a commissioner of the revenue; whether they reach the Title 3.2 dog license tax, which is paid on application, was not established, so they are not listed as an escalation route.

Treasurer agents. State law lets the Treasurer appoint agents and substations to sell licenses (§ 3.2-6527). No Staunton agent (for example a shelter or veterinary office) was found; the page names only mail and the Treasurer's office.

Rabies vaccination cost is set by veterinarians or clinics and is not stated by any City source. State law requires each city to see that a rabies clinic is held at least once every two years (§ 3.2-6521(B)); no current Staunton clinic schedule was found. The Shenandoah Valley Animal Services Center site (svasc.net) was not read.

Privacy. The Treasurer page names the elected Treasurer and links a personal mailbox, the Paying Taxes & Fees page puts the Treasurer's name in its mailing address, and the court pages name clerks and judges. None of these is recorded. No general Treasurer email address was found. The only email recorded is the Animal Control mailbox, which the Animal Control page publishes as the office channel.

Sources. State law quotes are matched to Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, not to the law.lis.virginia.gov pages linked in each citation. The regulation, the 12VAC5-105 forms list, the Virginia Courts pages and the Virginia Department of Health pages were read live on 2026-10-11. The exemption form PDF itself has not been checked; its title and link come from the 12VAC5-105 forms list.

All City pages read were captured between February and July 2026. Fees and procedures change with City Council action; check the Treasurer's Dog License page or call 540.332.3833 before relying on them.

Summary: the dog needs a current rabies vaccination 'or a health department exemption' (12VAC5-105-30(B); Va. Code § 3.2-6521(F)).

s3: added the regulation's condition for an exemption (vaccination would likely endanger the animal's life because of a previously diagnosed disease or documented medical considerations). Replaced 'with the dog's medical records', which overstated the rule: the veterinarian submits the form and any other documents or records the health director asks for (12VAC5-105-30(B)). Two regulation quotes added to legal_basis.

s5: 'There is no city application form' is now 'The Dog License page names no application form' (no source says none exists). The suggested note no longer asks for a phone number and the dog's name, which no source requires. It now lists only what the license receipt records under § 3.2-6527 (owner's name and address, the dog's sex and spay or neuter status).
s7: 'may ask for proof' is now 'may require information showing that from any applicant', as § 3.2-6527 says.
s8: added that it is unlawful to let a licensed dog 4 months or older run or roam at large without its tag (§ 3.2-6531), with a legal_basis quote.

s9: the step had limited the Treasurer's 90-day follow-up to dogs 'vaccinated in the city'. § 3.2-6529 also has other treasurers pass on certificates for dogs of owners living elsewhere, so it now says that. The deadline field no longer reads as a 90-day deadline for the owner: the follow-up does not extend the 30-day deadline of § 3.2-6530(A).
s12: the kennel definition is labelled as the state one (§ 3.2-6500); the City Code's definition was not read.

Penalties: added legal_basis quotes for § 3.2-6587(A) (Class 4 misdemeanors), (A)(7) (concealing or harbouring a dog whose license tax is unpaid) and (A)(9) (any other violation without a specific penalty, which covers owning an unlicensed dog under § 3.2-6524(A)). The penalties caveat is rewritten to match, and it says which subdivision or City Code section a Staunton summons would cite was not confirmed.

Fees: added the two impound fees on the Animal Control page that had been left out: $15 for a dog without a current rabies vaccination, and $25 for a dog found running at large. All five listed impound fees are now in fees.

Escalation (impound rung): added that a dog not claimed by the end of the hold period is deemed abandoned and becomes the shelter's property (§ 3.2-6546(D)), with a legal_basis quote. The basis now cites (C) and (D).

Caveats: the impound caveat now records the eCode360 Article III headings §§ 6.10.210, 6.10.220 and 6.10.230 (impoundment; prosecution of owner redeeming dog), text not read. The payment caveat now notes the older in-person card statement that sits in an HTML comment on the Paying Taxes & Fees page, is not displayed, and was not relied on.
open_issues: The live city site (www.ci.staunton.va.us) blocks the research User-Agent with HTTP 403, so every city page was read from Internet Archive copies no newer than 2026-07-17. The text has not changed since at least November 2021 (and is confirmed identical in September 2025), but the live pages could not be confirmed.

The Staunton City Code (eCode360) was not read beyond section headings, because of eCode360's terms. So the tax rates, the due date, the late-payment rule, the kennel and duplicate-tag fees, and the section that sets the impound fees are not confirmed from the ordinance. The fees given come from the Treasurer's and Animal Control pages.

The Dog License page's renewal rule ('by Jan. 31 of the year the rabies vaccination certificate expires') does not say when a license ends. s10 gives the page's words and the caveat flags the ambiguity. Ask the Treasurer's office.

Not stated by any source read: which payment types the Treasurer's counter takes for dog licenses, who checks are payable to, whether to mail the original rabies certificate or a copy, the kennel license fee, the duplicate-tag fee, whether Staunton exempts retired police or military dogs (§ 3.2-6528(B)), and whether Staunton licenses cats.
